coelenteron.d: the saclike body cavity of a coelenterate

coefficient.d: a constant number that serves as a measure of some property or characteristic

coercion.d: using force to cause something to occur

coelostat.d: optical device used to follow the path of a celestial body and reflect its light into a telescope; has a movable and a fixed mirror

coevals.d: all the people living at the same time or of approximately the same age

coenzyme.d: a small molecule (not a protein but sometimes a vitamin) essential for the activity of some enzymes

coerce.d: to cause to do through pressure or necessity, by physical, moral or intellectual means :

coeliac.d: of or in or belonging to the cavity of the abdomen

coenobitic.d: of or relating to or befitting cenobites or their practices of communal living

coenobitical.d: of or relating to or befitting cenobites or their practices of communal living

coeducational.d: attended by members of both sexes

coeducation.d: education of men and women in the same institutions

coelacanth.d: fish thought to have been extinct since the Cretaceous period but found in 1938 off the coast of Africa

coequal.d: having the same standing before the law

coelenterata.d: hydras; polyps; jellyfishes; sea anemones; corals

coelom.d: a cavity in the mesoderm of an embryo that gives rise in humans to the pleural cavity and pericardial cavity and peritoneal cavity

coelophysis.d: one of the oldest known dinosaurs; late Triassic; cannibalistic

coelogyne.d: any of various orchids of the genus Coelogyne with: clusters of fragrant lacy snow-white flowers; salmon-pink solitary flowers; chainlike racemes of topaz and chocolate brown flowers; spikes

coelenterate.d: radially symmetrical animals having saclike bodies with only one opening and tentacles with stinging structures; they occur in polyp and medusa forms

coextensive.d: being of equal extent or scope or duration

coefficient of concordance.d: a coefficient of agreement (concordance) between different sets of rank orderings of the same set of things

coefficient of friction.d: the ratio of the weight of an object being moved along a surface and the force that maintains contact between the object and the surface

coefficient of reflection.d: the fraction of radiant energy that is reflected from a surface

coefficient of self induction.d: the ratio of the electromotive force produced in a circuit by self-induction to the rate of change of current producing it, expressed in henries

coefficient of absorption.d: a measure of the rate of decrease in the intensity of electromagnetic radiation (as light) as it passes through a given substance; the fraction of incident radiant energy absorbed per unit m

coefficient of correlation.d: a statistic representing how closely two variables co-vary; it can vary from -1 (perfect negative correlation) through 0 (no correlation) to +1 (perfect positive correlation)

coenobite.d: a member of a religious order living in common

coefficient of elasticity.d: (physics) the ratio of the applied stress to the change in shape of an elastic body

coefficient of viscosity.d: a measure of the resistance to flow of a fluid under an applied force

coefficient of drag.d: the ratio of the drag on a body moving through air to the product of the velocity and the surface area of the body

coefficient of expansion.d: the fractional change in length or area or volume per unit change in temperature at a given constant pressure

coefficient of mutual induction.d: a measure of the induction between two circuits; the ratio of the electromotive force in a circuit to the corresponding change of current in a neighboring circuit; usually measured in henrie
